---
title: "Air Quality at RDU Airport, 2018–2020"
output: word_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center")
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
source("R/clean_air_quality.R")

air_2018 <- process_air_quality("data/AQ_2018.csv")
air_2019 <- process_air_quality("data/AQ_2019.csv")
air_2020 <- process_air_quality("data/AQ_2020.csv")
air <- bind_rows(air_2018, air_2019, air_2020)
air$year <- factor(format(air$date, "%Y"), levels = c("2018", "2019", "2020"))
air$month <- factor(month.abb[as.integer(format(air$date, "%m"))], levels = month.abb)

make_table <- function(data) {
  data.frame(
    Pollutant = c("CO (ppm)", "PM2.5 (ug/m3)", "O3 (ppm)"),
    Minimum = sprintf("%.3f", c(min(data$co, na.rm = TRUE),
                                min(data$pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
                                min(data$o3, na.rm = TRUE))),
    Maximum = sprintf("%.3f", c(max(data$co, na.rm = TRUE),
                                max(data$pm25, na.rm = TRUE),
                                max(data$o3, na.rm = TRUE)))
  )
}
```

## Data cleaning

I removed duplicate rows and changed negative values to 0 before calculating daily means. The order matters because duplicates can change the means.

## Daily concentration ranges

```{r table2018}
kable(make_table(air_2018), caption = "Table 1. Daily concentrations in 2018", align = "lrr")
```

```{r table2019}
kable(make_table(air_2019), caption = "Table 2. Daily concentrations in 2019", align = "lrr")
```

```{r table2020}
kable(make_table(air_2020), caption = "Table 3. Daily concentrations in 2020 (Jan–Apr)", align = "lrr")
```

## CO and ozone by month

```{r plot1, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.4, fig.cap="Figure 1. Monthly means and 95% confidence intervals for CO and ozone."}
monthly <- air %>%
  select(month, co, o3) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(co, o3), names_to = "pollutant", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(month, pollutant) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(!is.na(value)),
            avg = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            s = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(lower = avg - 1.96 * s / sqrt(n),
         upper = avg + 1.96 * s / sqrt(n),
         pollutant = factor(pollutant, levels = c("co", "o3"),
                            labels = c("CO (ppm)", "Ozone (ppm)")))

ggplot(monthly, aes(month, avg, color = pollutant)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ pollutant, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Month", y = "Mean concentration") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

I used two panels because CO and ozone have different scales.

## PM2.5 by month and year

```{r plot2, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.8, fig.cap="Figure 2. Monthly mean PM2.5 by year."}
pm_monthly <- air %>%
  group_by(year, month) %>%
  summarise(pm25 = mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(pm_monthly, aes(month, pm25, color = year, group = year)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(x = "Month", y = "Mean PM2.5 (ug/m3)", color = "Year") +
  theme_minimal()
```

I used lines to show how PM2.5 changed from month to month.

## Interpretation

CO was generally higher in fall and winter, while ozone was higher in spring and summer. PM2.5 was lower in early 2020, but the highest daily PM2.5 value was also in 2020. Since 2020 only has data through April, we cannot compare the full year.
